question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom.

At sixes and sevens
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"at sixes and sevens"** means to be in a state of confusion or disorder.
 
• It is used to describe a situation where things are not in their usual order or are in a chaotic state.
 
• The origin of this idiom dates back to the 14th century and was initially used in gambling contexts.
 
• Over time, its usage has evolved to describe general disarray.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Example Sentence:** *"After the sudden resignation of the manager, the office was **at sixes and sevens**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "Heavy rains"** – This is not related to the idiom "at sixes and sevens."
 
• **Option 2: "In happy mood"** – This option is incorrect as it does not convey the meaning of disorder or confusion.
 
• **Option 4: "Having dispute"** – Although disputes can cause disorder, this option does not capture the full meaning of the idiom
